intro: The neuter lo: lo de, lo plus adjective plus que, lo mío, and the set phrases built on it.
p.lo de ayer.consejo: «Lo de» + noun points to a matter both know about: «siento lo de ayer».
p.lo de la mudanza.consejo: «Lo de la mudanza» sums up the whole matter without repeating details. The z sounds «th».
p.lo bien que.consejo: It adds force: «mira lo bien que canta». With adverbs, «lo» never changes form.
p.lo cansada que.consejo: The adjective agrees: «lo cansada que estoy» (woman), «lo cansado que estoy» (man).
p.lo importante.consejo: «Lo» + adjective turns a quality into an idea: «lo importante», «lo mejor».
p.lo mío.consejo: It can be your affairs or your talent: «cocinar no es lo mío». With «tuyo»: «lo tuyo».
p.por lo visto.consejo: It is used when telling something you have heard or seen: «por lo visto, no viene».
p.por lo menos.consejo: You can also say «al menos». It shows a minimum amount.
p.por lo general.consejo: Synonym: «en general». The g sounds like h: por lo he-ne-RAL.
p.lo antes posible.consejo: It never changes: «lo antes posible». It equals «cuanto antes».
p.imaginarse.consejo: It is pronominal: «me imagino», «no te imaginas». The g sounds like h: i-ma-hi-NAR-se.
p.salón.consejo: It has an accent: sa-LON. In the plural, «salones», without accent.
b1.texto:
**Lo** is the neuter article. It never stands before a noun.

- **lo** + adjective makes an idea: **lo bueno**, **lo importante**, **lo mejor**.
- **lo de** + noun, infinitive or adverb points at a matter both speakers know about: ¿sabes **lo de** Ana? Siento **lo de** ayer. **Lo de** trabajar en casa me gusta.
- **lo** + adjective or adverb + **que** means how, with force. The adjective agrees: no sabes **lo cansada que** estoy. Mira **lo bien que** canta. Me sorprende **lo caras que** son.
- **lo** + possessive is my thing, your thing: la cocina no es **lo mío**.
- **lo que** is what.

Set phrases: **a lo mejor**, **por lo menos**, **por lo visto**, **por lo general**, **lo antes posible**, **a lo lejos**.
b2.f2.texto: Don't worry. The important thing is that we've talked about it.
b2.f3.texto: You can't imagine how tired I was.
b2.f4.texto: Apparently, the business of the move has been hard.
b2.f6.texto: But look how well the living room has turned out.
b2.f7.texto: At least now we have a place to rest.
b2.f8.texto: I want to paint the walls as soon as possible.
b4.texto:
- **lo + adjective**: lo difícil es empezar (the hard part)
- **lo de + noun**: ¿sabes lo de Ana? (the business about Ana)
- **lo + adjective + que**: no sabes lo cara que es (how expensive it is)
- **lo + possessive**: cantar no es lo mío (my specialty)
- **lo que**: no sé lo que quiere (what he wants)
b4.e1.texto: As a rule, my aunt arrives early.
b5.f0.texto: In the morning, the new living room smells of fresh paint and clean wood.
b5.f1.texto: The moving boxes form crooked towers next to the wall.
b5.f2.texto: Noelia opens a window and lets in the best of the day.
b5.f3.texto: Apparently, the afternoon light always reaches that corner first.
b5.f4.texto: A golden ray falls on the floor and lights up the dust like a tiny rain.
b5.f5.texto: As soon as possible, she wants to hang a large painting above the sofa.
b5.f6.texto: As a rule, new houses take a while to feel like homes.
b5.f7.texto: This afternoon, the living room already has a voice of its own.
b5.f8.texto: Noelia imagines the winter afternoons by the stove, with a blanket over her knees.
b5.f9.texto: She does not know how good she is going to feel there.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: you report something you have heard or seen.
b6.o1.refuerzo: No: it does not speak of what you see right now.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It has nothing to do with someone having seen it.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «lo de» + noun points at the matter.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Lo que» needs a verb after it, not «ayer».
b7.o2.refuerzo: Here «ayer» takes no article: «lo de ayer».
b7.pregunta: Complete the matter both of you know.
b8.frase: Mira lo bien que ha quedado el salón
b8.traduccion: Look how well the living room has turned out
b9.frase: No sabes lo ____ que son las casas.
b9.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the adjective agrees in feminine plural.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It is masculine singular and does not agree with «casas».
b9.o2.refuerzo: It is singular, but «casas» is plural.
b11.o0.refuerzo: That would be «la cocina no es mía».
b11.o1: cocinar no se me da bien
b11.o1.refuerzo: Well done: «lo mío» is what you are good at.
b11.pregunta: «La cocina no es lo mío» means…
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «lo» + adjective makes an idea, «the hard part».
b12.o1.refuerzo: «El difícil» would be a difficult man or masculine thing.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «La difícil» would be a difficult woman or feminine thing.
p.gritado.consejo: Participle of «gritar», to shout. Stress on TA: gri-TA-do.
p.imaginas.consejo: From «imaginar», to imagine. The g before i is h: i-ma-HI-nas.
p.duro.consejo: Here it means tough or hard. Stress on DU: DU-ro.
p.tía.consejo: Feminine, «la tía». The accent on the í breaks the diphthong: TI-a.
p.torres.consejo: Plural of «torre», tower. The rr is strong: TO-rres.
p.torcidas.consejo: Feminine plural of «torcido», bent. The c before i is th.
p.casas.consejo: Plural of «casa», house. Stress on KA: KA-sas.
p.tardan.consejo: From «tardar», to take time. Stress on TAR: TAR-dan.
p.parecer.consejo: Infinitive of «parecer», to seem. The c before e is th in Spain.
p.estufa.consejo: Feminine, «la estufa». Stress on TU: es-TU-fa.
p.sentirse.consejo: «Se» at the end is part of «sentirse», to feel. Stress on TIR.
